newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Kraft Jacobs Suchard not to use gene soya.
newsitem.headline: Kraft Jacobs Suchard not to use gene soya.

text.p: Leading chocolate company Kraft Jacobs Suchard SA (KJS), a unit of Philip Morris Inc, said on Friday it would not use genetically-modified soybeans in its European products for now.
But it was not opposed to the controversial bean on safety grounds.

"In a number of countries we found the regulatory situation regarding modified soya and foodstuffs was uncertain. We decided therefore that any products that contain soya or derivatives will for now be sourced from normally grown soya," Cynthia von Maerestetten, KJS's director of European affairs told Reuters.

She denied the company's action was linked to a campaign against genetically-modified soy by environmental group Greenpeace over health. Greenpeace have held up shipments of new crop U.S. soybeans to Hamburg and Antwerp as part of this protest.
Von Maerestetten said, however, that KJS had no doubts over the safety of the soy.

"On the contrary, we think the modified soya and ingredients from it do not pose a problem. Certainly all the scientific and regulatory authorities who have looked at it have concluded the same thing," she said.
She declined to comment on where KJS sourced its soy or name the countries where KJS believed there were doubts over the legal framework governing genetically-modified soa.
